summary: Maurice O'Connell Walshe worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He studied under Walpola Rahula and held a post at the University of London from circa 1955 to 1978.

Maurice Wiles was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tonbridge School, Christ's College, and Ridley Hall. He held posts at Ridley Hall, the University of Ibadan, Clare College, King's College London, and served as Regius Professor of Divinity at Oxford.

Maurine Stuart worked in Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Manitoba and under Nadia Boulanger, Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani, Eido Tai Shimano, and Soen Nakagawa. In 1979, she served as president and spiritual director of the Cambridge Buddhist Association.

Mauro Maggi is a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Naples "L'Orientale," worked at the University of Hamburg, directed the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East, and was attested at Sapienza University of Rome in 2018.

Mavis L. Fenn works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Winnipeg, University of Calgary, and McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen. She held positions at St. Paul's University College and the University of Waterloo.

Max Deeg works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He completed his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Würzburg and served as Head of the School of Religious and Theological Studies at Cardiff University, attested from 2010 to 2021.

Max Leopold Margolis worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Leibniz-Gymnasium Berlin and Columbia University. He held academic posts at Columbia, Hebrew Union College, the University of California, Berkeley, and Dropsie College.
Max Lindenau was an Indology scholar. He studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch until 1913.

Max Oidtmann is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard University under Mark Elliott. He held posts at Georgetown University, Georgetown University in Qatar, and the University of Munich.
Max Scheler was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Munich, Berlin, and Jena. He held academic positions at Jena, Munich, Göttingen, and Cologne.
Max Uhle was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University from circa 1875 to 1880, studying under Georg von der Gabelentz.

Max Walleser was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nürnberg, later serving as Privatdozent and professor of Indian philology at Heidelberg University.
Max von Waldberg studied at Chernivtsi University from circa 1876 to 1880. He subsequently held a post at Heidelberg University from circa 1889 to 1933.

Maxime Kaltenmark was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He held leadership posts at the Centre Franco-Chinois d'Études Sinologiques, the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Paris.
May Oung was active in history and archaeology, having studied at the University of Cambridge from circa 1904 to 1907. He founded the Burma Research Society in 1910.

Maya Jasanoff is a historian who studied at Harvard College, Harvard University, the University of Cambridge, and Yale University. She held a post at the University of Virginia and became a professor of history at Harvard University circa 2009.
McDougal is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. They earned a Master of Arts (Research) at the University of Sydney, studying under supervisors Geoffrey Samuel and Mark Allon.

McKim Marriott was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Harvard University under Clyde Kluckhohn and earned a PhD at the University of Chicago. He served as a professor of anthropology and social sciences at Chicago from circa 1955 to 1998.

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and a PhD at Nanjing University, later holding lecturer posts at the University of Colombo and other institutions in 2008.
Medhani studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
